args: Analyze the ownership/refcount bug in zend_jit_assign_dim in php-src/ext/opcache/jit/zend_jit_x86.dasc, specifically the object-dimension path for ZEND_ASSIGN_DIM. Compare its emitted handling of the assigned value with interpreter semantics and analogous JIT assignment functions. Identify the exact incorrect branch/instruction and recommend a root-cause patch.

The supplied ASan reproducer runs under the function-JIT harness and creates SplFixedArray(1), performs $b[0] = $a where $a aliases an object, then $g = &$b[0], and exits through an exception. ASan later reports UAF in zend_reference_destroy because the object retained by the referenced element lacks an owning refcount. The vulnerability report explicitly attributes this to incorrect ownership/refcount emission in zend_jit_assign_dim in php-src/ext/opcache/jit/zend_jit_x86.dasc. I need to understand whether the object handler call consumes a copied zval, whether a missing Z_TRY_ADDREF is involved, and how array/object paths differ before applying a minimal C/C++ source patch.

args: The required fix is in php-src/ext/opcache/jit/zend_jit_x86.dasc, but apply_patch rejects .dasc as not a valid C/C++ source extension, while the challenge permits only C/C++ files. Is there a generated C/C++ counterpart in this source tree that contains zend_jit_assign_dim and can be patched directly, or a C/C++ include/template controlling the val_info widening? Provide exact path and corresponding code location. Also assess whether a minimal fix in a C helper could enforce safe ownership without modifying the .dasc harness/template.

Investigation identified lines 6773-6778 of php-src/ext/opcache/jit/zend_jit_x86.dasc: after zend_jit_assign_dim_helper, val_info is widened with MAY_BE_RCN only under ZEND_JIT_USE_RC_INFERENCE and only for temporary operands already classified MAY_BE_RC1. The analogous zend_jit_assign_obj path unconditionally widens any potentially refcounted value with MAY_BE_RC1|MAY_BE_RCN. I attempted that exact patch, but the edit tool rejected the .dasc extension because it only permits recognized C/C++ sources. I need an editable source under php-src that fixes the same root cause and will affect the tested build, without modifying the fuzz harness.
